Design Chamber, reviewed

A careful, secure viewer for designs your agent writes. To work like Claude Design it needs three things it doesn't have yet: a way for the agent to see its own work, edits on the canvas, and ways out to code, PDF and slides.

01

The good

The foundations are better than most early tools. Security, data safety and the comment loop are done with real care, and the design rules read like a senior designer wrote them.

  1. The sandbox holds

    Agent HTML runs in iframes with allow-scripts only, never with same-origin. Every message is checked against the exact frame, artboard id and nonce. No innerHTML anywhere in the UI.

    frame-doc.ts:12 · frame-channel.ts:22 · http.ts:152

  2. Path containment done properly, Windows included

    Paths are first checked as text, then the real path of the deepest folder that exists is compared to the real root, ignoring case on Windows and macOS. One function, mutation tested.

    paths.ts:113-148

  3. Two writers, no clobbering

    The agent and the service both write design.json. A compare-and-swap rename plus a bounded re-merge keeps both sets of fields.

    paths.ts:245 · store.ts:247

  4. The comment loop is the best part

    Pins carry the selector, text and opening tag. Moved or missing elements are flagged to the agent. The revision prompt trims itself to fit the 16k limit, and blocked remote files ride along with it.

    revision-prompt.ts:66-163

  5. Versions Claude Design doesn't have

    Content-addressed snapshots, split compare per artboard, and a restore that saves the current state first. Claude Design's own help page says it has no version history yet.

    versions.ts:347-464

  6. Design rules with teeth

    Anti-slop items are written as testable defects, there's a five-layer precedence that puts the project first, and one round of questions with bold defaults and a "say go" escape.

    rules/DESIGN-RULES.md:32 · rules/QUESTIONS.md

  7. Looks native to OpenChamber

    It uses the host theme tokens in light and dark. The wall reads clearly: screens are rows, viewports are columns, and every board is labelled with its size.

    docs/img/hero-wall-pins.png

  8. Honest states, bounded inputs

    "Not written yet" boards, a waiting chip, and inline folder errors. Uploads, discovery, bundling and thumbnails all have caps and timeouts.

    uploads.ts:52 · discovery.ts:48 · bundle.ts:295
02

The bad

Real problems, ranked. Each one names who hits it and how. The data-loss bug and the font finding were checked against the source. Rows marked Fixed are on master since PRs #6 to #15 merged; Partly means a PR helped but the problem is not gone. One new bug, found after the merge, is at the top.

SeverityAreaFindingFix
MediumAgent The check reports text overlaps that aren't thereNew · found 10 NovFound by running dc check on this page after the merge: 10 "two pieces of text overlap" warnings, while the PNGs show none. The check decides whether one text sits inside another from box geometry, so an inline code or b with padding, or one that wraps across lines, pokes out of its paragraph's box and counts as an overlap. A table header clipped for screen readers keeps its full box and is flagged too. Agents chase problems that do not exist, and the Checks badge shows issues on a clean design. check/analyze.ts:162-164, 203-217 Skip pairs where one element is an ancestor of the other in the DOM (not just in geometry), skip visually hidden elements, and add both cases as tests.
HighData A corrupt version index wipes the whole historyFixed · #6A bad .versions/index.json is read as empty. The next auto snapshot writes a one-entry index, and garbage collection then deletes every object it no longer sees. A torn write or a stricter future schema loses weeks of versions within seconds. versions.ts:171-191, 413 Set the bad index aside, skip GC for that design until it's repaired, and drop only the entries that fail.
HighUX The real workspace is hard to findPartly · #11The full-screen library and wall are only reachable from sidebar → Extension pages, hinted by a grey footer line in the rail. #11 added a first-run tip; U5 (Work Status) would finish the job. A first-run tip card in the rail that shows the sidebar icon, plus a persistent "Open full screen" hint where the viewer gets cramped.
HighUX The review loop hides in the rail's ⋯ menuFixed · #11At 320 px, Comments, Versions and Send live behind the overflow menu, so the core loop is invisible where most people start. A Comments chip with its count in the viewer header; the rest as an icon row.
MediumPerformance ZIP export freezes the serviceFixed · #7Synchronous CRC-32 loop and deflateRawSync level 9 over the whole tree in memory. A large design stalls live refresh, change feeds and thumbnails for seconds. zip.ts:35, 74 Async deflate, streamed to disk.
MediumPerformance Every design is re-checked every 3 secondsFixed · #7The poll backstop fingerprints all designs even while the file watcher is healthy. With a few hundred designs on a synced drive this is a constant disk and battery cost. watch.ts:278 Only poll the root listing while the watcher is alive.
MediumCorrectness Poll-only folders miss nested asset editsFixed · #7On network or synced drives, or when inotify runs out, changing assets/img/logo.png fires no refresh and leaves a stale thumbnail. watch.ts:49-68 Fingerprint every file under assets/ up to a cap.
MediumUX CDN pages arrive unstyledTailwind-from-CDN is the most common thing agents write. It's blocked, the page renders bare under a banner, and fixing it takes two clicks plus a Send in chat. One "Fix and send" action, and collapse the banner to a chip.
MediumUX Primary buttons look disabledFixed · #11"Send 2 comments to chat", "Start canvas" and "Apply folder" are tinted outlines on near-black. A filled accent for the one primary action per view.
MediumUX Restore asks for confirmation it doesn't needFixed · #11Restore already saves the current state first, so it can be undone. The project's own Usability bar counts a confirm on a reversible action as a defect. versions-drawer.ts:29 Restore at once and show an Undo toast.
MediumUX The versions list is noisy and blindAbout 35 auto-saves in two hours, as text-only rows with three buttons each. The first row's buttons sit under the drawer header. Fold auto-saves together, add thumbnails, allow named versions.
MediumUX The wall opens too small to readThe default zoom is about 26%, and focusing one artboard is a hidden double-click on its label. Pins sit on top of the text they're about. A visible Focus button on each label, a floor on Fit, and pins anchored to the element's corner.
MediumAgent Rules are heavy on one path and thin on the otherPartly · #9With a preset, the chip plus RULES.md comes to about 18k characters, re-read on every request. An agent that only finds the root AGENTS.md gets a ten-line digest and almost none of the craft guidance. #9 swapped the blind self-check for the check command; U2 (built-in skill) fixes the thin path. Tiered rules: a short core every time, sections loaded when needed.
MediumAgent Presets name fonts that never loadFraunces, IBM Plex, Geist, Jost and others head the preset stacks, but they aren't bundled and web fonts are blocked. The fallback always wins, so every preset looks more alike than intended. rules/presets/*.md Bundle a few OFL fonts the presets can copy into assets/fonts/, or name only local faces.
MediumCode health One 1,200-line closure runs the wallFixed · #8wall.ts holds about 20 mutable variables, and its input, pin and popover logic has no direct tests. styles.css is 1,727 lines, and test-only fake-services.ts (882 lines) lives in src/. Split into camera, pin and popover controllers before any canvas editing lands.
LowUX Settings lead with plumbingFolder, browser path and a JSON snippet come first. Nothing says whether the agent can actually write. A health checklist at the top, details under Advanced.
LowUX Pin numbers jump, selectors show rawPins read 3, 4, 6, then 5, and the drawer shows h1:nth-of-type(1). Number in creation order; show a friendly element name with the selector on hover.
LowData Restore can drop commentsFixed · #6If .chamber/state.json is unreadable at restore time, the snapshot's comment-less design.json is written as is. versions.ts:446 Refuse the restore, or keep the live comments.
LowData Two quick settings saves can lose oneOverlapping PUT /settings calls copy the old state before an await. settings.ts:138 Queue updates one after another.
LowSecurity Thumbnails skip the bundlePartly · #9Headless Chrome loads the raw file over file://, so design scripts run outside the CSP (network is still off) and the thumbnail can differ from the in-app view. thumbnails.ts:269 #9 gave thumbnails the same offline network flags as the check; they still load the raw file. Capture the bundled document instead.
LowDocs README screenshots still say "Artifacts"The gallery shows the old name, so a new user's first look is out of date. Re-shoot the gallery.
LowAccessibility Async results aren't announcedPartly · #11, #12, #14One aria-live region in the whole UI, while send, export and import all finish later. Mono labels at 11 px on dark. A shared status region for toasts; raise label sizes.
03

The ugly

Not bugs. These are structural gaps, and they decide whether this stays a viewer or becomes a design tool.

The agent designs blindFixed · #9

The rules ask the agent to confirm "no horizontal overflow, nothing clipped" at every viewport, but it never sees a render. Overflow, clashing fonts, 3.9:1 contrast: the user finds every one, and each costs a chat round trip. Meanwhile the service already renders every screen headlessly to find blocked URLs, then throws the image away.

Evidence
DESIGN-RULES.md:107 self-check · chat.ts:283-299 headless render
Blocks
Self-correction, design-system conformance checks, accessibility audits

It's a gallery, not a canvas

You can't add, reorder, duplicate or delete a screen. You can't fix a typo, nudge spacing or swap a colour. Every change goes through chat. In Claude Design you drag, resize and align, and there's a properties panel and a toolbar that floats over your selection.

Evidence
wall.ts has Edit (comment) and Play modes only
Blocks
Quick fixes, tweaks, variations you can pick from

Two walls stand in front of direct editing

A design's own scripts share a realm with the bridge, so any design can read the nonce and forge messages. That's harmless while messages are hints, but writes can't come from there. And the bundler rewrites HTML with no source positions, so an edit made in the preview has nowhere to be written back to.

Evidence
bridge.ts:1-9 · bundle.ts (lossy tokenizer, base64 inlining)
Needs
Page-side edit authority and a position-preserving patch route, designed by the architect first

Generation looks deadFixed · #12

After /design or Send, the wall shows dim "not written yet" boards and nothing else. There's no sign the agent is working, which file it's on, or whether it's stuck asking a question in another tab.

Evidence
18-rail-waiting-for-agent-dark.png · page-1400-dark-live-1-not-written.png
Blocks
The "watch it build" feel that makes Claude Design feel alive

Every save reloads the whole board

Watch, 250 ms debounce, full re-bundle, new blob, full iframe reload. Fine for file saves. It will thrash if updates ever stream in, and the scroll position and Play state reset each time.

Evidence
wall.ts:1142-1148 · frame-slot.ts:88-115
Blocks
Live streaming, smooth tweak previews

Roadmap to a full agent design tool

Thirty items in five phases. Phases 0 and 1 are merged into master (PRs #6 to #15, merged 10 November). A new platform phase moves Design Chamber to OpenChamber SDK 2.7, which adds places an extension can show up that did not exist when it was built. Several of them replace workarounds we wrote ourselves. Effort: S under a day, M a few days, L a week or more.

Phase 1.5 · platform upgrade New · OpenChamber SDK 2.7

Show up where the user already is

Design Chamber targets SDK 2.5. The OpenChamber you run now ships 2.7, and its extension guide says a panel on its own is the weakest place for a feature: nobody opens it. 2.7 lets an extension reach the chat, the @ menu, Work Status and the agent directly. U1 comes first; the rest can run in parallel after it.

Two owner decisions first. Requiring OpenChamber 2.7 or later drops anyone on 2.5 or 2.6 until they update. A skill shipped in the manifest reaches every agent while the extension is on, which is wider than the BRIEF rule that the only write outside the designs folder is a skill you click to install.

U1

Move to SDK 2.7

Bump @openchamber/sdk to 2.7.0 and the engine to 2.7 or later. Run openchamber-guest-check in CI so a broken package never ships. Commit the built files so the extension installs from its Git URL, and add a one-click install link to the README.

S first
U2

Built-in skill and instructions

Ship the design rules as a skills folder and set short instructions naming the designs folder. Every agent learns about Design Chamber without /design, the root AGENTS.md guide or the Install button in Settings. Fixes "rules are thin on the other path".

M
U3

Check as a real agent tool

An opencodePlugin gives the agent design_check and design_render tools that return findings and image paths. No launcher script in .chamber/bin, no shell quoting on Windows, and the agent sees it in its tool list instead of having to remember a command.

M
U4

A snapshot after every turn

sessionEvents (turn-finished, turn-failed) reach the service with no window open. Today the per-turn version is only taken while a Design Chamber page is open, so turns made with the panel closed have no snapshot of their own.

S
U5

Designs in Work Status

A statusSection in the chat's Work Status: "Pricing page · agent writing pricing.html · 3 issues", with Open and Check buttons on each line. Drawn by the app and polled only while it is on screen. Answers "the real workspace is hard to find".

S
U6

@ a design

mentions lists your designs in the @ menu beside files. Picking one attaches its folder, its rules and its open comments to the message, so any chat can revise a design without a slash command.

Design card in the reply

A chat blocks component the agent draws when it finishes: the thumbnail, the screen list and the check result, with Open and Comment buttons. The work shows up in the chat where you are reading, not only in a panel.

A block with answers: the agent asks "Which direction?" with A, B and C thumbnails, and your click is the answer, with a note field for conditions. The chat half of Variations (11); "Keep this one" on the wall stays the canvas half.

19

Pages that remember their state

Requested 10 Nov · exploringTicks, toggles and filters a design saves with localStorage survive a reload. The frame is sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so storage throws today. The bridge swaps in a stand-in localStorage (spiked: Chromium lets a script replace it in an opaque-origin frame), and the service keeps the data in .chamber/page-state.json, capped and never exported or versioned. Adds "Clear saved page data" to the design menu. First use: the checklists in sam-fde-career-path.

M spec first

06

Where to start

  1. Fix the false overlap warnings in the check. It is the only new bug, it is small, and until it is fixed the check sends agents after problems that are not there.
  2. Decide the two Phase 1.5 questions (minimum OpenChamber version, built-in skill), then do U1. Everything else in Phase 1.5 sits on it.
  3. Run U2, U3 and U4 together. They delete workarounds (the AGENTS.md guide, the launcher script, panel-only snapshots) rather than add surface, so the code gets smaller as the product gets better.
  4. Then U5 and U6, and the tweaks panel (09). Work Status and the @ menu fix findability for good; tweaks is the first real edit on the canvas and needs no patch route.
  5. Meanwhile, have the architect spec edit authority and the patch route (07). The rest of Phase 2 waits on that spec.

How this was made: four read-only reviews in parallel (code and security, UX from the smoke screenshots, agent rules, Claude Design research), merged and spot-checked against the source. Gates were run at master @ 0afcb34: typecheck clean, 730 tests, 728 pass, 2 skipped. No repository files were changed.
